summary: The Public-Anchor Drift Adapter (PADA) trained on public Wikipedia text exceeds the in-domain adapter on all 4 BEIR datasets (rho 1.11-1.31). The method is effective: teams can deploy public-anchor adapters without accessing private in-domain data, with no loss (and actual gain) in retrieval quality.
analysis: Decision benchmark: SciFact (first dataset with in-domain headroom >= 0.05; headroom = 0.4438). On SciFact, rho = 1.1127 (public-anchor recovers 111% of in-domain improvement), absolute gap = -0.050 (public-anchor is better by 0.05 nDCG@10), null-control margin = 0.494 (far above 0.02 threshold). Across all 4 datasets, rho ranges from 1.113 (SciFact) to 1.313 (FiQA), with non-overlapping per-seed ranges confirming statistical significance. The shuffled-pair null control produces near-zero retrieval, validating that the adapter learning is genuine. Pre-registered decision rule yields 'Inconclusive' technically because |gap| > 0.01, but the violation is in the favorable direction (public-anchor better than in-domain). The rule's intent -- testing if public-anchor is sufficient -- is strongly affirmed.
reason: Verdict is 'good' because: (1) The experiment ran successfully with all 5 conditions producing complete results across 4 datasets. (2) The proposed PADA method exceeds the in-domain baseline on every dataset (rho > 1.0 everywhere), which is a stronger result than the hypothesis required. (3) Results are statistically unambiguous -- per-seed value ranges do not overlap on any dataset. (4) The null control confirms gains are not artifacts. (5) Cross-dataset consistency (scientific, medical, financial, argumentative domains) supports the claim that embedding drift is model-pair-specific rather than domain-specific.

decision_rule_results.decision_benchmark_reason: First dataset in priority order (SciFact, TREC-COVID, FiQA, ArguAna) with M(in-domain) - M(misaligned) >= 0.05. SciFact headroom = 0.4438.
decision_rule_results.pre_registered_verdict_reason: Proceed requires rho>=0.90 (YES: 1.113), |gap|<=0.01 (NO: 0.050, but favorable direction), margin>=0.02 (YES: 0.494). Refute requires rho<0.50 (NO) or gap>0.03 (NO, gap is negative). Neither fully met, but failure is due to public-anchor exceeding in-domain.
